is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates insecticide resistance in Anopheles arabiensis and Anopheles gambiae s.l. in western Kenya (Page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes Vgsc L1014F (L995F), L1014S (L995S), and Ace-1 G119S (G280S) (Page 5, Table 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 on page 6 reports the sample sizes (N) and allele frequencies for L1014, L1014S, L1014F, and G119S across different years and zones.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were reared from larvae collected from irrigated and non-irrigated fields in Homa Bay County, western Kenya (Page 1, Page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study describing field collections, bioassays, and molecular genotyping.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study was conducted in specific irrigated and non-irrigated clusters in Homa Bay County, western Kenya (Page 3, Fig. 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Larval collections were conducted between February and July in 2018 and 2019 (Page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study was supported by NIH ICEMR grants, but describes routine primary field collections unique to this study.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype frequencies and sample sizes are reported in Table 2 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study assessed insecticide resistance and target-site mutations (Vgsc L1014F/S and Ace-1 G119S) in Anopheles arabiensis from irrigated and non-irrigated areas of Homa Bay County, western Kenya, in 2018 and 2019. Low frequencies of kdr mutations (1-16%) and Ace-1 G119S (0.7%) were detected.
